title: Birbal and the Painter (हिन्दी)
summary: A miserly merchant refuses to pay a portrait painter by constantly altering his facial expressions. Birbal provides the painter with a flawless remedy. [HI]
full_text:
A talented portrait artist of Agra was commissioned by a notoriously stingy merchant named Seth Chhaganlal to paint his portrait for fifty silver rupees. The artist labored for three weeks, capturing every nuance of the merchant's features—his sharp nose, arched eyebrows, and embroidered silk turban.

When the portrait was unveiled, the cunning merchant decided he did not want to part with his silver. He sneered, 'This looks nothing like me! Look at my cheeks—they are fuller than this! Repaint it, or I shall not pay a single dam!'

The patient painter took the canvas back, adjusted the cheeks, and returned. But Chhaganlal had shaved his beard and narrowed his lips, claiming again: 'A terrible failure! The jawline is completely wrong!'

The artist painted three different portraits over two months, but on each visit, the dishonest merchant deliberately changed his facial expression, puffing his cheeks, squinting his eyes, or altering his mustache, refusing to pay. Exhausted, bankrupt, and on the verge of starvation, the poor artist went weeping to Birbal.

Birbal listened to the painter's plight and said with a comforting smile: 'Do not despair, my friend. Tomorrow, go to the merchant's mansion and tell him you have prepared a portrait that will mirror his exact likeness at every second of the day, never failing to match him. Take this draped object with you, and I shall accompany you.'

The next day, Birbal and the painter arrived at Chhaganlal's mansion. The merchant smirked: 'Have you finally painted my true face?'

'Yes, Sethji,' the artist said, unveiling the object.

It was an exquisite, polished silver mirror!

Chhaganlal glared at the reflection. 'What mockery is this? This is only a mirror!'

Birbal stepped forward: 'Does this mirror not capture your exact likeness? When you smile, does it not smile? When you puff your cheeks, does it not puff? Since your face changes every morning like the shifting clouds, only a mirror can paint your true portrait!'

Turning to Emperor Akbar, who had arrived to witness the resolution, Birbal added: 'Now let the merchant pay the artist one hundred rupees—fifty for the portrait, and fifty for the artist's stolen time!'

Akbar roared with laughter and enforced the payment, warning the miser never to defraud honest artisans again.
